"), developer of the SOLO™ Micro-Modular Reactor, today announced significant progress in the industrial manufacturing program for its SOLO™ reactor, following a series of technical and operational activities with key Italian industrial partners

") and Boldrocchi.

The activities included manufacturing-process development and factory preparation for the first-of-a-kind (FOAK) SOLO™ reactor at ATB, as well as hot-running testing of critical helium circulation equipment at Boldrocchi. Together, these milestones demonstrate the Company's continued transition from engineering design toward manufacturing execution and physical system integration, supporting its targeted FOAK deployment next year.
Key Highlights:
First-of-a-Kind Manufacturing: Terra Innovatum and ATB advanced preparations for SOLO™ reactor assembly, including development of manufacturing procedures and evaluation of dedicated factory space.
Industrial Process Validation: The companies are establishing manufacturing trials to validate the assembly methods and production processes intended for SOLO™ construction.

Critical Equipment Testing: Terra Innovatum oversaw a four-hour hot-running test of a helium circulator at Boldrocchi, advancing qualification activities for a key component of SOLO™'s helium cooling system.
System Integration: Two additional helium blowers are being prepared to support non-nuclear testing of helium circulation equipment and system interfaces.
ATB Advances Industrial Manufacturing Preparations for SOLO™

Terra Innovatum and ATB have progressed their joint industrial manufacturing program, focusing on the processes, infrastructure and assembly methods required to construct the first SOLO™ Micro-Modular Reactor.

At ATB's manufacturing facility, the companies conducted technical and operational working sessions addressing the practical execution of reactor assembly, including manufacturing-process verification, production workflows and factory layout.

The teams are establishing a series of manufacturing trials designed to validate the assembly procedures that will be employed in SOLO™ production. These activities are intended to translate engineering specifications into practical, repeatable industrial manufacturing processes.

The companies also evaluated factory space and production configurations for the assembly of the first SOLO™ reactor, an important step in supporting the Company's targeted deployment of its first-of-a-kind reactor next year, in 2027.

ATB's established industrial manufacturing capabilities provide Terra Innovatum with access to specialized infrastructure, production expertise and quality-control practices to support the transition toward reactor manufacturing.

The collaboration reflects Terra Innovatum's strategy of leveraging experienced industrial partners and proven manufacturing methods rather than developing new manufacturing infrastructure from the ground up.
Boldrocchi Conducts Helium Circulation Equipment Testing
In parallel, Terra Innovatum progressed its critical equipment qualification program with Boldrocchi, a specialist in industrial air and gas handling systems.
At Boldrocchi's facility, Terra Innovatum's technical team oversaw a four-hour hot-running test of a helium circulator of the same design intended for installation in the SOLO™ helium cooling loop.
The testing represents a tangible step in evaluating equipment integral to the reactor's thermal management system and supporting its integration into the broader SOLO™ architecture.
Additionally, two helium blowers are being prepared for use in a system testing facility.

The equipment will support system-level testing of helium circulation performance and interfaces, providing important engineering data and operational experience to support the integration of critical reactor components.

These activities reinforce Terra Innovatum's approach of utilizing established industrial technologies and working with experienced equipment manufacturers to streamline development and reduce execution risk.
Building the Foundation for Scalable Reactor Production
The progress achieved with ATB and Boldrocchi reflects Terra Innovatum's focus on establishing an industrial manufacturing model capable of supporting the commercial deployment of SOLO™ reactors.

Unlike development approaches dependent on fundamental technology breakthroughs, Terra Innovatum's strategy emphasizes the integration of established technologies, qualified components and proven manufacturing capabilities into a standardized, factory-built reactor platform.
The Company's ongoing work spans critical equipment testing, system integration, manufacturing-process validation and preparation for first-of-a-kind reactor assembly.

Collectively, these activities are establishing the technical and industrial foundation for repeatable manufacturing, a central element of Terra Innovatum's strategy to deliver scalable, commercially deployable nuclear power solutions.
Alessandro Petruzzi, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Terra Innovatum

, commented: "We are moving beyond engineering design and into the practical industrial work of building SOLO. With our first-of-a-kind reactor targeted for deployment next year, the work underway with ATB and Boldrocchi represents tangible progress toward that milestone.

"What makes our approach particularly compelling is that we are leveraging established industrial capabilities rather than attempting to invent an entirely new manufacturing ecosystem. ATB and Boldrocchi bring decades of relevant engineering and manufacturing expertise, and our collaboration is now producing tangible progress.
"We believe this industrial execution model is a fundamental competitive advantage for SOLO and an important foundation for our long-term objective of manufacturing and deploying reactors at scale."
Marco Cherubini, Co-Founder, Chief Technology Officer and Product Director of Terra Innovatum
, added: "Our work with ATB and Boldrocchi is focused on the practical details of manufacturing and integrating the critical systems of the SOLO reactor.

"At ATB, we are developing and validating the assembly processes that will be used to manufacture SOLO. At Boldrocchi, we are conducting equipment-level testing and preparing helium circulation components for system integration activities.

"These are tangible engineering and manufacturing steps that move us closer to construction of our first reactor and help establish the repeatable industrial processes that will support subsequent units."
ABOUT TERRA INNOVATUM & SOLO™
Terra Innovatum is advancing innovative, sustainable nuclear energy solutions through the
SOLO™ Micro-Modular Reactor

. Conceptualized in 2018 and engineered over six years by experts in nuclear safety, licensing and R&D, SOLO™ is designed for efficient today’s world commercial deployment; using readily available commercial components to reduce supply-chain risk and improve cost predictability. Running on the only commercially available and non-proliferant fuel LEU, its flexible platform is designed to support LEU+ and transition to future fuel options, including HALEU.

SOLO™ is designed to provide CO₂-free, behind-the-meter and off-grid consistent power and heat for data centers, remote communities and energy-intensive industries including cement, oil and gas, steel and mining, desalination, water treatment and co-generation, as well as defense installations. Its modular architecture can scale from individual units of 1MWe to deployments of 1 GW or more, while also supporting specialized applications such as medical radioisotope production.
